LESSON: READING 6.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Technology Suggested vocabulary Computer, record, type, information, internet, e
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Fluency, part of Technology Suggested vocabulary Computer, record, type, information, internet, e in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: what you have read in a personal journal. 1. How should we read? 2. What benefits do we get in reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Pick out words with letter-sound combinations: /dr/, /gr/, /shr/, from a chart. Learners with speech difficulties can pick out orally, by typing or writing.  Blend target sounds to read words with target letter-sound combinations, with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication  Read words with letters-sound combination correctly,

2. Read a text displaying the right facial expressions and tone. Learners with speech difficulties could read at their level of functional ability.  Engage in timed reading with peers taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks,  Practise reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words,  Participate in reader’s theatre and record

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  Pick out words with letter-sound combinations: /dr/, /gr/, /shr/, from a chart. Learners with speech difficulties can pick out orally, by typing or writing.  Blend target sounds to read words with target letter-sound combinations, with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication  Read words with letters-sound combination correctly,
2. Read a text displaying the right facial expressions and tone. Learners with speech difficulties could read at their level of functional ability.  Engage in timed reading with peers taking appropriate pauses at punctuation marks,  Practise reading sentences containing decodable and non-decodable words,  Participate in reader’s theatre and record

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is heightened as they record what they have read in a personal

journal.

 Collaboration: Teamwork is developed as the learner participates actively in timed reading with peers, observing the rules of

engagement.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates the effort of others as they engage in timed reading and give positive feedback.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is boosted as they read texts fluently.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the reading fluency skills acquired when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.
